children: By Mike Scarcella

The American Veterinary Medical Association persuaded a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit by one of the largest U.S. veterinary schools alleging it abused its authority as an educational accreditor to suppress the number of veterinarians and protect its members from competition.
Here are the details:
In his

on Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Thomas Varlan in Knoxville, Tennessee federal court said Lincoln Memorial University had not adequately shown how it was being harmed and that its lawsuit was too speculative to move ahead now.

Lincoln Memorial last year alleged the American Veterinary Medical Association violated U.S. antitrust law through restrictive accreditation standards that threaten the availability of veterinary services and make animal care more expensive.
The veterinary trade association represents more than 100,000 veterinarians. An internal arm of the association sets criteria that schools must meet and maintain for accreditation.

Lincoln Memorial’s lawsuit challenged its probationary accreditation, saying that the designation at its Tennessee campus harmed its ability to expand and hurt its reputation. The school sought an order restricting the association from applying its accreditation standards.
The association in

of the case argued Lincoln Memorial’s lawsuit was premature since there’s been no final decision about accreditation. Varlan in his order said Lincoln Memorial’s speculation about the future accreditation status of its Tennessee program “may never come true.”

The U.S. Justice Department last year filed a “statement of interest” reflecting the views of the federal government in the case. In a statement on the filing, it said "professional accreditation associations “cannot erect anticompetitive hurdles that reduce competition by restricting the number of veterinary providers entering the profession.”

In a statement on Wednesday, Liberty Memorial University said the court's ruling was not on the merits of the allegations, and that the Justice Department supported its position in the case. The university also said it “remains poised to vindicate its claims in the future as necessary.”
The case is Lincoln Memorial University v. American Veterinary Medical Association, U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Tennessee, No. 3:25-CV-00282-TAV-CRW.
For plaintiff: Thomas Thagard III of Maynard Nexsen
For defendant: Cameron Regnery and J. Cole Dowsley Jr of Freeman Mathis & Gary
